Commentary.Commentary: So that is it from this game! We do have a decider. Who will take the series? Join us to find out on Sunday at 2000 local - 0000 GMT (6th August, Monday). Till then, take care and goodbye.

Bangladesh captain, Shakib Al Hasan says after the loss in St. Kitts, they had a chat which evoked belief that they can beat the Windies. Thanks the crowd for the support they have shown and he hopes they provide the same support in the next game as well. Ends by saying all the bowlers bowled really well and all-in-all, it was a complete team effort.

Man of the Match, Tamim Iqbal says that in the previous game, he got out off the first ball but the shot was on. Adds that he took his time today and it worked for him. Applauds Shakib Al Hasan and says that he got in, played some shots and took the pressure off him, which helped him as well. Ends by saying that the pitch is amazing, he loves it and he is enjoying his first outing in Florida.

Windies captain, Carlos Brathwaite starts by saying he was pretty content with his decision as they took wickets early on and put Bangladesh under pressure in the first half. Adds that they slipped due to the casual fielding efforts which allowed the opposition to claw back in the game. Implies that they will look to finish off the contest in the next game. Asserts that Denesh Ramdin's dismissal was a bit questionable but these things happen in the game. Ends by saying that the team is confident and will look to get back to winning ways sooner rather than later.

Well, when you look at the stats, not many teams win when they lose three in the Powerplay but Fletcher and Powell's 58-run stand turned the tide in favor of the Windies. The two were going great guns before the former threw his wicket away. Shakib then along with Rahman bowled exceptionally well at the death, giving Islam 14 runs to defend in the final over. The left-arm spinner did not disappoint as he bowled a magnificent 20th over ensuring the last T20I is not a dead rubber.

Bangladesh have drawn level! An excellent collective effort by them. First, it was their experienced pair of Shakib and Tamim who bailed them out of trouble with a 90-run stand and then they carried the momentum onto the field and have managed to defend the target. Mustafizur, who is so highly regarded in this format, came to the fore. He struck early, not once but twice, removing the two most dangerous Windies batsmen, Russell and Lewis. Shakib then joined the party by removing Samuels and Windies were three down in the Powerplay itself.

That is it! BANGLADESH WIN BY 12 RUNS! Just 2 given in the last over and to top that, Islam has also taken two wickets. Brilliant by him. He fires this full again on middle, Badree hits it down to long on for an easy run.

OUT! TIMBER! What an outstanding last over this has been from Islam. 0,1,W,0,W. Sees the batsman make room, so he fires it full on the stumps. Paul swings but misses to see his stumps get shattered. You miss I hit stuff. Samuel Badree will replace him.
Another dot! It is surely over now. If it wasn't before. Full and on the pads, the batsman swings but gets hit on the pads.
Kesrick Williams is the next man in to bat.

OUT! High up in the air... taken! Game, set and match for Bangladesh. Islam tosses this up on middle, Ashley tries to clear mid-wicket but it does not go the distance. He holes out to Haque who dropped one earlier but takes this. The Bangladeshis are ecstatic.
He should have done this a ball before as he hits it down to long on for a run. 14 from 4. Big hit needed, the man who can go big is now on strike.

A dot to begin. No Paul, when you have someone striking the ball really well, you should not be swinging but giving the strike to him. Islam fires this on the pads, Paul swings but misses. A dot to begin, 15 from 5 needed.
15 needed off 6 balls as Nazmul Islam comes to bowl the penultimate over.

FOUR! 16 from the over and the game is going right down to the wire. Windies are still well in it. A ball shorter in length outside off, Nurse goes for the cut but gets a bottom edge past the short third man fielder.

SIX! Nurse is not going to go down without a fight. What a shot. Full and outside off, Ashley goes down on one knee which helps him get the elevation. He lofts it over covers and the ball carries all the way.
The batsman plays the pull shot. They pick up a single.
Keemo Paul is the next man in.

OUT! Powell departs and he probably takes the hopes of the Windies of chasing this target down back with him. Rahman persists with the short ball outside off, Powell goes for the pull but gets a top edge. Rahim times his jump, gets a hand to it but fails to hang on. He does really well to keep his eyes on the ball and takes it on the second attempt.

FOUR! BOOM, BOOM GOES POWELL! What a hit! Not the right length by Rahman. Too short by him. Powell says thank you so much and pulls it over square leg for a boundary. If there is one man for the Windies who can do it, it is him.
A cutter on middle, the batsman tucks it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Mustafizur Rahman to bowl out.

In the air... dropped! Should have been taken considering the high standards Shakib sets for himself. A fuller slow ball outside off from Hossain, Powell looks to power it down the ground but the bat turns in his hand. As a result, the ball lobs in the air towards covers. Shakib there runs to his left, gets under it but fails to hold on to the catch even after a dive. A brace results in the end.
Powell goes after a wide one and misses.

Brilliant stuff from Rubel. Another yorker outside off, Nurse tries to scoop it but could only get it to point. The batsmen run for a single and the fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end. A close run results as the ball doesn't hit the stumps.
Yorker outside off, Powell digs it to the on side and takes a quick single.
Full on off, driven through covers for a single.
Wide! Outside the tramline outside off, wided.
Full on leg, hoicked away to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Rubel Hossain is back for his final over.

Yes he does! Again only a run. A wicket and just three from this over. Shakib did it with the bat before and he has done a commendable job with the ball too. 4-0-19-2 is what his figures read. His last ball has been pushed towards covers for a run. 39 needed in the last 3.
Just a single from the penultimate ball of this over as it is flicked through square leg. One ball to go, need to bowl it well.

Flighted ball on off, Powell pushes it back to the bowler. Excellent stuff this from Shakib, bringing all his experience into play. Varying his pace really nicely. 2 balls left, need to finish it well.
Flatter on the pads, Powell tries to defend but misses to get hit on the pads.
Ashley Nurse Walks in next.

OUT! What a catch! Wow! Liton Das, you beauty. Shakib tosses this one up on middle, Brathwaite lofts it towards wide long on. He too, like many others in this game, gets more height than distance. There are two fielders converging towards it, one from long on and the other from deep mid-wicket. Das, from the latter position, keeps his eyes on the ball and avoids the collision with the other fielder. He takes it above his head and then also maintains balance to stay inside the field. Brilliant. Brathwaite can't believe it as he walks back and Bangladesh are now favourites here as they have got the dangerous Windies skipper. 41 more needed in 22.
Very full on middle, Powell swings but gets an inside edge towards short fine leg for a run.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on.

SIX! Was that a cricketing shot or a forehand? Well, whatever it was, it was effective. Another short ball angled across Brathwaite, he flat bats it and deposits it into the long on stands. Equation down to 42 off 24.
One for the over signals the umpire. Carlos fails to make connection with the short ball.
Short again, pulled off the inner half to mid-wicket for another single.
Powell goes for the pull but misses it completely.
Short around off, pulled to mid-wicket for a run.
On a length, slower leg cutter, Powell moves across to hoick it over mid-wicket but an upper edge behind point earns him a single.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on.
Flatter on off, guided to point. So an expensive over but a wicket from it. 51 in 30.
Swept and swept well! This is floated up on middle, Brathwaite goes down on one knee and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary. Off the mark in style.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Works it with the turn through mid-wicket for a run.
Carlos Brathwaite makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! In the air... gone! Fletcher what have you done? Was this really needed? Especially after hitting a maximum on the first ball. This wicket has once again brought the match right in the balance. Credit to the bowler here, he shows courage by tossing it up on middle, Fletcher tries to play across the line and that is his undoing. The ball turns, takes the top edge and goes towards Shakib at point who does not drop it. So, Fletcher does not make the most of the life he was given. An uncharacteristic innings by him comes to an end.

SIX! Dealing in maximums are Windies here. A delightful shot by Fletcher. Islam tosses this up on off, Fletcher goes inside out with the turn, overs covers and clears the rope. Pressure on the bowler.
Nazmul Islam is back on.
Nope! He did try but this was cleverly bowled! Slower ball and on the fuller length outside off. Powell swings but misses.
SIX! Back-to-back biggies and Powell slowly turning things on here. A full toss and Powell just lofts it over the long on fence. So 14 from the over so far, can Powell make it an 18 run over or more?
SIX! BANG! Powell goes big and he clears the fence. This is should probably get him going. A length ball on the stumps, Powell gets into position and pulls it over the mid-wicket fence.
Slower ball outside off, Powell tries to cut but is beaten by the low bounce. So just 2 from the first 3 balls.

DROPPED! And the bowler is not at all pleased by that. He lets out a loud roar as soon as that was dropped. Haque is the culprit. The slower short ball on middle, Andre goes for the pull but does not get the desired elevation. It goes towards deep mid-wicket where the fielder runs to his right and then spills it. The batsmen take one. Can Fletcher do what Tamim did after he was dropped? Windies will surely hope.
That was in the slot. Full and on off, Powell misses out as he can only hit it to long on for a run.
Abu hider is back on.
A single to end as Powell eases this to long on. The required rate is almost 11 now.
FOUR! Much, much-needed. A poor ball to be honest. Short and wide outside off, Powell tries to cut but gets an outside edge past the keeper and into the fence.
A full toss on middle, Fletcher fails to put it away as he gets it off the inner half towards deep mid-wicket and the batsmen take a run.
A dot! Another over which is turning out to be a good one. Full and on off, Fletcher smashes it to mid off.
Back of a length on off, Powell pushes it through covers for another single.
Back of a length on middle, AF pulls it down to long on for a run. The Windies need to go now. Singles won't do the job for them.
Rubel Hossain is back on.

Even the edges are not finding the fence. Shakib floats this up on off, Powell swings but the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards third man for a couple. Another very good over, 84 needed in 48.
Driven towards the mid off region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Another single! Bangladesh won't mind this as Powell mistimes his pull towards deep square leg.
Fires it on middle, Fletcher mistimes the pull towards mid-wicket for a run.
Slower through the air but way outside off, left alone and it has been wided.
Quicker and on off, AF pushes it towards cover.
Flatter on off, Fletcher punches it back to the bowler.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single. Just 6 from the over, very good in this format.
Shortish and outside off, Fletcher goes for the cut but misses.

In the air... but short! Excellent slower ball on off, Powell is foxed by it as he goes for a drive. He is way too early into the shot as it goes uppishly towards covers. There are shouts of catch it but it lands well short of the fielder.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side. They pick up a single.

FOUR! Full marks to the bowler there but runs to the batsman. On a length around off, coming in with the angle. Powell tries to block but the ball takes the inside edge and goes through short fine leg for a boundary. Windies need a few more of these.
Shortish in length on off, Powell pushes it back towards the bowler who makes a good stop jumping to his right.
Yorker from the spinner and Fletcher digs it out back to him. 96 needed in the last 10 overs for the Windies.
Andre defends it from within the crease.

SIX! Boom! Out of nowhere, a massive pull from Fletcher. It isn't that short, but he rocks back quickly and middles it over the long on fence. The ball goes into the crowd and hits one of the spectators on his head. Poor guy!
Wide! Wide outside off stump, Andre leaves it alone. Wide signalled by the umpire.
Shortish around middle and off, Fletcher pulls it to wide long on. The fielder in the deep runs to his right and saves a couple for his team.
Hangs back and punches it to long on for a run.
Walks out of his crease and pushes it to mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Nazmul Islam is back on.
Another slower ball from Hider and another drive through covers for a run. 5 runs off this one.
Worked to long on by Powell for another easy single.
Abu rolls his fingers over this one, Fletcher pushes it through covers and takes a run.
Pulls the shortish ball to mid-wicket and changes strike.
Punches the fuller ball to covers for nothing.
On a length on the pads, Fletcher misses the line and the ball hits him on his pad. An appeal ensues but the umpire ignores it. The ball rolls towards the on side and a leg bye is stolen.
Abu Hider comes back for another spell.
Powell shoulders arms to let that one through. Bangladesh are in the driver's seat currently and are steering this game.
Full, slingy from Hossain, Powell looks to chop it but fails to do so.
On a length around off, played with soft hands to the off side for a quick single.
Shortish outside off, cut through point for a run.
Powell shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
In comes Rovman Powell.

OUT! What a review! Rubel has the hawk's eye to see that. He bowls a length ball around off and pushes it into Ramdin who tries to flick it but misses to get hit on his pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Hossain is convinced that it is hitting and he convinces his skipper as well. The review is taken. The replays roll in. No edge there and it hits him right in front of the sticks. However, the off pole is visible but tell you what, the ball is hitting the middle of leg stump. After having a look at the replays on the big screen, Rubel was walking back to his bowling mark convinced that it was going to miss the leg stump or it will be an umpire's call. To everyone's surprise, it's a successful review from Bangladesh.
Review taken! Hossain has convinced his skipper to go for it. Ramdin is the man in question regarding an LBW decision.
Wide! Ramdin tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side but misses. Wide signalled by the umpire.
Rubel Hossain is back on.
Drives the full ball to covers. Misfield from the fielder there allows Ramdin to take the single. Another tight over from Shakib.
Wrists the tossed up ball on off through mid-wicket and changes strike.
Fuller outside off, driven down to long off. One run taken.
Lunges forward to block it out.
Slower through the air around off, played to the off side and the batsmen scamper for another single.
Flighted around middle and leg, worked to square leg for a run.
Just a single as Ramdin pushes it down to long! So, just 4 from the last over of the Powerplay. 120 more needed.
On the shorter side, stays a touch low. Ramdin punches it back to the bowler. 2 dots.
Tosses this up on off, Ramdin drives it back to the bowler.
Fires this on the stumps, the batsman eases it towards wide mid on for a single.
Down the leg side, Ramdin flicks it towards short fine leg for another single.
Flatter on off, the batsman taps it towards covers for a run.
Spin from both ends! Nazmul Islam is into the attack.
Flicked to fine leg. End of Shakib's first and it is a successful one.
Ramdin gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.

OUT! What a catch! A short delivery around middle and leg, Samuels heaves it powerfully towards deep mid-wicket. He has made good connection which means Das in the deep has a chance of getting under it. However, he has to run in and put in a dive forward to complete the catch. The Bangla Tigers are ecstatic and Windies are losing the plot here.
Works it to mid-wicket and changes strike.
Fends the flatter ball and gets an inside edge onto his bat.
FOUR! Shot! Tossed up ball, Fletcher leans ahead and drives it through covers to find the fence.
Shakib Al Hasan is on.
SIX! Outta here! What a shot from Samuels. A length ball in line of the stumps, Samuels gets his right leg out of the way and lofts it into the crowd for a maximum.
FOUR! Edged and four! A fuller ball outside off, Samuels throws his bat at it and gets an edge. The ball runs between the slip fielder and keeper and races to the fence.
Marlon Samuels is in next.

OUT! Gone! Fizz has the last laugh. A short ball from around the wicket, Russell shuffles a touch to pull it over mid-wicket but only manages get a faint edge to the keeper. Rahim behind the sticks takes the catch and appeals. The umpire has no problem in giving that out. A huge, huge wicket for Bangladesh.
FOUR! Top edge but safe! A slower length ball angled across Russ who throws his bat at it and gets an upper edge. The ball goes over the point fielder for a boundary.
Wide! Too wide outside off, left alone by Andre.
Russell opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man.
SIX! Oh my word! He has tonked that outta here. A swat from Russell for a 103 meter six. So easy! Rahman bowls a short ball outside off, Russell powers it over mid-wicket for a maximum.
FOUR! The runs are starting to flow now. 16 from the over. 150 more needed in 17 overs. Short again outside off, Fletcher makes room and hits it through backward point for a boundary.
Full on middle, Russell hits it hard towards mid on for a run.
SIX! BANG! Brute force! Slightly short on middle and Russell pounces on it. He pulls it and the timing is such that it goes all the way over the mid-wicket fence.

Another ball on the shorter side, Fletcher goes for the pull but is beaten by pace. The ball hits the inside edge and hits him on the body. It rolls beside the pitch and the batsmen run through for a quick single.

FOUR! That has gone to the fence like a tracer bullet. This should get the Windies going. Fletcher dances down the track and he gets a short ball outside off. The batsman cuts it through point and the ball races to the fence in no time.
Slightly short on middle, Fletcher pulls it to the man at mid-wicket.
Rubel Hossain is on.
Extra bounce here. Russell doesn't shy away from playing the pull to the short ball but fails to make connection. The 10 ball over comes to an end resulting in a wicket. Not too bad, eh!
Quick and short in line of the stumps, Russell keeps it out off the back foot.
Bouncer! Russell does well to evade it.
Swing and a miss from Russell. A length ball outside off, Russell fails to make connection.
Wide!  Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone. Wide signalled by the umpire.

OUT! Gone! Windies have lost their only review as Rahman strikes. A length ball pitching outside off, it comes back in with the angle as Lewis tries to defend but is struck right in front of the sticks. The bowler appeals and the umpire obliges by raising his finger. After some discussion with Lewis, Fletcher urges him to take the review as he feels that height can be a factor which he indicates to him. The southpaw agrees eventually. The replays roll in. The Snicko doesn't spot anything. The Hawk Eye now shows three reds. Another failure for Lewis. Early strike for Bangladesh, just what they wanted.
Review time! Lewis has been given LBW but his partner asks him to go for the review and he does so. Looks out to the naked eye.
Corrects his line this time and balls a shortish ball in line of the stumps. That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
Wide! My word, Rahman hasn't found his line as of now and dished out three wides in tandem. It's again down the leg side and Lewis misses it again.
Wide! Similar delivery from Rahman and it goes down the leg again. Wide signalled.
Wide! The ball is way wide on the leg side but Evin still goes after it. The Umpire signals a wide.
Mustafizur Rahman to bowl from the other end.
Lewis defends it from within the crease. They pick up a single. End of a good over from Hider, just 2 off this one.

Just in! Pressure was piling up and Fletcher took the risk eventually. A fullish ball around off, he punches it to covers and takes off for a run. Shakib comes charging in from the same region and hits the bull's eye at the striker's end. The square leg umpire takes it to the third umpire. The replays shows that Lewis made it in time by sliding his bat in. One run completed in the end.
A run out decision is taken to the third umpire. It looks like Lewis is short.
Played to the point region by Fletcher. He is yet to get off the mark.
Guides this one to third man for nothing.
Ooh! So close! Almost chopped it on. Hider bowls a fuller ball outside off, swinging it in to the right-hander. Fletcher throws his bat from his crease and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Shortish ball first up outside off, punched to covers by Fletcher.
We are back for the chase! Abu Hider has the new ball in hand and he will be bowling to Andre Fletcher. Here we go...
